lessons.title: Meet the Lower Tees
lessons.enquiry: How does the lower River Tees link land, water, people and the sea?
lessons.objective: I can locate the lower Tees, identify an estuary and explain one physical–human connection.
lessons.inherited: Week 8 closed the migration unit: retrieve map movement, key and what maps hide. Acknowledge the report-back if available; if it is not available, the named adult states its status or reasoned boundary, then this new enquiry begins.
lessons.feedsNext: Week 10 treats the river as a transport destination and connection.

lessons.title: Rails Meet the River
lessons.enquiry: Why did the Stockton & Darlington Railway link coal areas to the River Tees when it opened in 1825?
lessons.objective: I can explain the railway’s principal coal purpose, its link to Stockton’s river port and the opening-day passenger evidence.
lessons.inherited: Week 9 lower-Tees route and port connection.
lessons.feedsNext: Week 11 shows how rail and river made an 1850 ironstone find more powerful.

lessons.title: The Iron Rush
lessons.enquiry: Why did ironstone found near Eston in 1850 change Teesside so quickly?
lessons.objective: I can explain how ironstone, mines, rail, river and ironworks formed a change chain.
lessons.inherited: Week 10 rail–river network and the 1825/1830 chronology.
lessons.feedsNext: Week 12 uses work, transport and production links to explain fast town growth.

lessons.title: A Town Grows Fast
lessons.enquiry: How did port, rail and iron help Middlesbrough grow so fast?
lessons.objective: I can use dated evidence to explain town growth without claiming the data tells the whole story.
lessons.inherited: Week 11 iron chain and the 1850 trigger.
lessons.feedsNext: Week 13 uses growth in people, work and movement to explain the need to cross a busy river.

lessons.title: Crossing the Steel River
lessons.enquiry: How did engineers help people cross a busy working River Tees?
lessons.objective: I can match a river-crossing problem to two different steel bridge solutions.
lessons.inherited: Week 12 growth meant more people, work and movement near the river.
lessons.feedsNext: Week 14 weighs industrial and engineering change beside the Tees’s nature story.

lessons.title: Industry and Nature: The Tees Story
lessons.enquiry: How can the Tees be both an industrial place and an important place for nature?
lessons.objective: I can combine industry and nature evidence to tell a balanced Tees story.
lessons.inherited: Weeks 9–13: river and estuary, rail and port, iron, growth and moving bridges.
lessons.feedsNext: The six-week unit closes; one bounded pupil choice sets the next local-enquiry question or display emphasis.
